collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a teen aged 14-17; in the story (name1)'s arm ends just below the elbow)

collection.description: A teen asks whether a villager's leather arm cuff could hold other things: experiment together, or ask how they came up with it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s left arm ends just below the elbow; (subject.he/she) was born that way. Years ago, (subject.he/she) designed a cuff of hardened leather that straps over it, with a slot that holds a fishing spear, a digging stick or a paddle. (subject.He/she) is very good with it. Today (friend) has been watching (subject.him/her) fish and wants to know if the cuff could hold other things.

choices.label: Ask How (subject.He/she) Came Up with It

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They spend an afternoon testing. The cuff can hold a torch, a scoop, a drum beater, and, after some work, a very large spoon. It cannot hold a coconut. (friend) tries several times. (subject) starts designing a new slot for the spoon. (friend) asks to help make it. By the end of the season, they've invented four new attachments, two of which are useful.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tells (friend.him/her). (subject.He/she) was about (friend)'s age, (subject.he/she) was tired of everyone telling (subject.him/her) how to hold a spear, and (subject.he/she) went off and figured out (subject.his/her) own way. It took a whole year and a lot of ruined leather. (friend) is impressed. "Can I see the first one?" (subject) laughs and digs it out of a basket. It's terrible. They both admire it.
